s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful lower extremity swelling and erythema with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful left lower-extremity swelling and erythema
Intermittent fevers, episodic night sweats, decreased appetite, and palpitations
Ill-defined, warm, confluent erythema, edema, and tender induration on the left calf
key_facts: 53-year-old Hispanic man
Incidentally noted bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses six months earlier
Denies trauma or injury to the leg
Mild lymphocytopenia, moderate anemia, elevated creatine kinase, elevated aldolase, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase
Peripheral-blood flow cytometry was unremarkable
CT and MRI of the leg revealed gastrocnemius myositis, extensive subcutaneous and superficial myofascial edema, and popliteal lymphadenopathy
No improvement with intravenous ceftriaxone for presumed cellulitis and pyomyositis
Punch biopsy of skin from the lower leg showed a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Atypical mononuclear cells on biopsy and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Leukemia cutis
shortlist.why_kept: Atypical mononuclear cells on biopsy and mild lymphocytopenia

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms, bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, and lack of response to antibiotics

shortlist.label: Panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous and superficial myofascial edema on imaging and skin biopsy findings

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic symptoms, atypical mononuclear cells on biopsy, and lack of response to antibiotics

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, systemic symptoms such as fevers, night sweats, and weight loss, along with laboratory findings of mild lymphocytopenia, moderate anemia, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase, are highly suggestive of lymphoma. The punch biopsy showing a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: Peripheral-blood flow cytometry was unremarkable, which makes leukemia cutis less likely

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The biopsy did not show granulomatous inflammation, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest vasculitis

rejected.label: Panniculitis
rejected.why: While the patient has subcutaneous inflammation, the presence of atypical mononuclear cells and systemic symptoms suggests a more systemic disease process

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: The biopsy did not show granulomatous inflammation, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest this rare condition
